description: A deletes the statement B edits - git's classic delete/modify conflict. Distinct from delete_vs_edit, where B deletes something A merely *depends on*: here the two edits target the same statement, so there is no merge to construct. A's intent is y == 2 (the statement gone), B's is y == 11 (the statement changed), and no program is both. Type I fires and git conflicts, so both tools flag it and a human resolves - the agreement case that matters, because it shows the semantic checker is not merely more permissive.
category: agreement (delete/modify — neither tool can merge it)
